label: The absence of the girls' voices

blocks.text: The girls in the juvenile files appear mostly as subjects, and rarely as narrators of their own lives. The archive speaks extensively about them through reports, assessments and legal observations, rather than through their own voices — adult perspectives shaped by supervision, moral judgment and institutional aims. These silences limit what can be known about how the girls themselves experienced care, discipline, "home", or separation from their families.

"Now everything is all right with me again. Or would I not be allowed to go back to Zeist after all... But then, in truth, I have no future either." — Alida Mathilda (Tilly) de Jong (1919–1944), pupil of Huize Dina

"The Huize Dina documents contained almost no traces of childhood noises — of laughter, of crying, of fights, of the small interruptions of everyday life. [...] Still, they presented the late childhood of these young girls, soon-to-be women, as a sequence of logged events." — Tzlil

"Even when the files provided intimate details about a certain girl, those were merely the outline of a person, not her inner world. It left us with silhouettes: figures, whose missing parts imagination had to fill in." — Amit
